findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The counts are consistent: 12 blocks with 14 compiled examples, 37 T3E4NS cases, 33 deferrals split 1/2/18/12 across their owners, and 11 proof files. Scope stays observer-only and excludes certification and closing. Two requirements stated in the spec Rules have no scenario and no planned lower-level proof. First, R4's ticket.md field-level freshness: identity, scope and done_when stay bound while status, phase and Work Log can change. Second, R1's rule that changing the candidate or a bound input during execution prevents success. For both, an implementation that breaks the stated contract would pass every planned check. Add discriminating proof for both before scenario approval.

R4 says T3E4NS ticket identity, accepted scope, exclusions, completion conditions and parent linkage stay bound regardless of status, phase, timestamp and Work Log changes. It also says an entire ticket file cannot be exempted. The intake review called this ticket-field freshness out as a clarification. Yet no scenario covers it, and the dimensions.md 'Verification freshness' row lists only source/config/toolchain/profile changes, unchanged-content commits and loaded outputs. Two implementations would pass every planned check: one that exempts all of ticket.md, and one that hashes all of ticket.md. The first keeps reporting 'current success' after T3E4NS's scope or done_when changes. The second marks evidence stale on every Work Log entry. Add freshness partitions to observer-freshness, plus at least one acceptance-level control: a scope or done_when edit refuses current success, and a status, phase or Work Log edit preserves it.

R1 says observation binds the committed candidate at request start, and a change to the candidate or any bound input during execution prevents success. No scenario covers this, and no dimensions row has a partition or lower-level matrix for it: 'Candidate readiness' and 'Execution isolation' cover only state before execution. So an implementation that resolves HEAD, toolchain or lockfile identity after the run, or never compares start and end identities, passes every named check. It could then issue a verifiable success that binds inputs other than the ones executed. Add this partition, for example a commit or bound-input change injected mid-run in observer-source-identity or observer-execution-environment, and state which identities are compared.

R1 says the required set comes from the observer's shipped, reviewed contract, not a project-edited census. The 'unmapped delivery case' scenario can be satisfied by either design: an observer that reads the project's .bdd-proof.json, or one that uses its shipped contract. Its Given is phrased so the project-file design is the natural reading. Dimensions only partly covers this: 'Request authority' lists caller overrides, and 'mismatched profile' appears only under candidate readiness. Name a lower-level case proving that a committed edit which removes or renames a required assertion in the project mapping cannot shrink the required set.

R5 says both successful and refused observations identify their meaning as execution evidence only. The R5 scenario and the observer-history-preservation row exercise only the successful path. Add a lower-level check, in observer-recovery-messages or history-preservation, that refused and interrupted results also carry the execution-evidence-only meaning and change no history.

The R4 refusal scenario ends with a request to 'observe the new committed candidate'. If the changed input is dirty rather than committed, the honest recovery action is to commit or clean first. The 'Diagnostics' row should make sure the one concrete recovery action matches that case.

Context only: in the T3E4NS .bdd-proof.json, three entries are flat [file, title] pairs while the rest are nested arrays: 'A malformed plan record…', 'Refused selectors…' and 'A failed independent attempt…'. proof-inventory.json normalizes these. Whatever shipped contract the observer derives must preserve them exactly, without depending on the project file's shape.
